sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- lens_diagnostics: lens_diagnostics source=session reads the session cache and an empty cache is not proof of a clean file; use source=lsp scope=paths for changed files when cached findings are absent or stale
- symbol_search: Find files by identifier
- effective_config: Explain resolved configuration
- project_report: Orient in a project before choosing a file
- module_report: Outline a source module before reading a body
- read_symbol: Read one symbol's body instead of the whole file
- read_enclosing: Read the enclosing symbol or callback body for a line
- pi_lens_activate_tools: Activate a situational tool
- subagent_gate: Run subagent tasks with bounded retries and a required success quorum
- workspace_session_summaries: Inspect same-CWD session summaries before potentially overlapping repository work
- subagent: Delegate focused work to child agents; compose multi-child work in one workflow call.
- subagents_enable: pi-subagents is installed. For authorized specialist, independent-review, or parallel work, call subagents_enable, then subagent. Authorization must come from the current request or applicable instructions; complexity alone is not authorization.
- ask_user_question: Ask the user up to 4 structured questions (2-4 options each) when requirements are ambiguous
- workflow: Delegate substantive independent or staged work to subagents with a JavaScript workflow, optionally composing agent calls with parallel(), pipeline(), or both
- workflow_control: Inspect and manage workflow runs directly by canonical run ID.

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Use subagent_gate instead of raw subagent calls when a delegated result must be retried safely or a success quorum must be enforced.
- Set each subagent_gate task retrySafety to read-only only when rerunning it cannot duplicate file mutations or external side effects; omission defaults to may-write.
- Use workspace_session_summaries when another Pi session in the same working directory may overlap the current work.
- After workspace_session_summaries, compare goals, files or symbols, decisions, and next steps; when overlap is material or ownership is unclear, coordinate through intercom before writing.
- Use ask_user_question whenever the user's request is underspecified and you cannot proceed without concrete decisions — you can ask up to 4 questions per invocation.
- Each question MUST have 2-4 options. Every option requires a concise label (1-5 words) and a description explaining what the choice means or its trade-offs. The user can additionally type a custom answer via the automatically appended "Type something." row on every question, or press Esc to abandon the questionnaire. Do NOT author "Other" or "Type something." labels yourself — reserved labels are rejected at runtime.
- Set multiSelect: true when multiple answers are valid. Provide an options[].preview markdown string when an option benefits from richer side-by-side context (mockups, code snippets, diagrams, configs) — single-select only. The "Type something." row is appended to every question; in preview mode it expands to the full pane width while typing so the custom answer is not cramped into the narrow options column. If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option and append "(Recommended)" to its label.
- Do not stack multiple ask_user_question calls back-to-back — group all clarifying questions into one invocation.
- The `workflow` tool runs multi-agent orchestration — it fans decomposable work out across subagents, and fits tasks shaped like: repo-wide inspection, independent parallel research/checks, multi-perspective review, or fan-out/fan-in synthesis. ONLY call it when the user explicitly opts in — via the workflow trigger word, `/workflows run`, or their own words (e.g. 'run a workflow', 'fan this out', '并行审一遍'). For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit — do not call it; you may briefly offer it (with a rough cost) as an option instead.
- Use workflow_control for workflow lifecycle management; do not ask the user to type /workflows when this tool can perform the action.
- Use stop to terminate or quit a run. Closing the navigator does not stop a run.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.description: Run a JavaScript workflow that delegates work to subagents with agent(), optionally composing calls with parallel() and pipeline().

Add phases: [{ title: 'Phase' }] only when the workflow has named phases, and declare only phases it will use. With multiple phases, call phase('Exact Title') before each phase's work or set `phase` in the agent options. Use `await workflow(savedName, childArgs)` to run a saved workflow inline; nesting is limited to one level and shares the parent run's concurrency, agent, and token limits. Optional quality helpers include verify(), judgePanel(), loopUntilDry(), and completenessCheck(). Optional control helpers include retry() and gate(); budget exposes total, spent(), and remaining(), and phase('Name', { budget: N }) sets a phase token limit. The optional `agentType` option selects a named user or project definition that can bind tools, a model, and role instructions; use it only when its name and purpose are provided in context. Its bound model overrides `tier`; an explicit `model` overrides both. Use plain JavaScript only; imports, require(), filesystem modules, Date.now(), Math.random(), and new Date() are unavailable. Use phase('Name'), agent(prompt, opts), parallel(arrayOfFunctions), pipeline(items, ...stages), log(message), args, cwd, process.cwd(), and budget. The workflow must call agent() at least once. parallel() requires functions, not promises, and returns results in input order: await parallel(items.map(item => () => agent(...))). pipeline(items, ...stages) runs stages sequentially for each item while items proceed concurrently; each stage receives (previousValue, originalItem, index).

# Implementation Plan — Clickable queue chip with queue-order popup

## Goal

Make the queue number in the UI clickable so it opens a popup showing the
execution queue in its current dispatch order (#1 runs next, then #2, …),
giving the operator a visual way to debug why the number "doesn't seem to
ever go down" when the dashboard only shows 2–3 tasks.

## Success Criteria

- Clicking (or keyboard-activating with Enter/Space) the queue chip in the
  bottom bar opens a popup listing the queue in its current dispatch order.
- Each row shows, at minimum: position (#1, #2, …), task name, project,
  current step, and blocked/waiting reason when applicable.
- The popup's contents reconcile with the chip number well enough to debug
  with: any deliberate count-vs-list difference is labelled in the UI, not
  silent.
- `npm run test:unit` passes; new unit tests cover popup open/close,
  ordering, empty/error states, and the chip's click behaviour.
- No long-lived dev servers are used for verification (headless runners /
  `npm run capture:screenshot` only).

## Current behaviour (researched, not assumed)

- The chip lives in the bottom-bar right rail
  (`frontend/src/components/layout/NowPlayingBar.jsx`, L638–666). It is
  currently a non-interactive `div role="status"` wrapped in an
  `InfoTooltip`, hidden on phones (`hidden sm:flex`).
- The number comes from `resolveUniversalNowPlaying`
  (`frontend/src/components/layout/activeTaskVisibility.js`, L93–126): it
  prefers `engineState.openQueueDepth` (global, all projects) and falls back
  to the loaded-list open count. `openQueueDepth` is assembled by
  `resolveEngineState` (`api/work/resolveEngineState.js`, L55–60) via
  `countOpenTasksGlobal` (`api/work/countOpenTasksGlobal.js`): every task
  whose status is neither `completed` nor `done`, across ALL projects —
  including `failed`, `waiting_human`, `paused`, and blocked tasks.
- This already explains the reported symptom: the dashboard shows the
  active-project slice (2 tasks) while the chip counts every open task in
  every project, including terminal-ish states like `failed` that never
  "go down" on their own.
- An ordered queue list already exists: `QueueOrderWidget`
  (`frontend/src/components/observability/widgets/QueueOrderWidget.jsx`)
  renders `scheduledQueue` with rank, project, priority reason, stage, and
  task key. The monitor feeds it from
  `api.observabilityStatus(...).observability.queue`
  (`frontend/src/components/observability/ObservabilityDashboard.jsx`).
- The canonical ordered source is `GET /tasks/queue`
  (`api/work/taskWorkRoutes.js`, L179–202) → `taskStore.getScheduledQueue`
  → `getScheduledQueue` (`api/flow/scheduler/getScheduledQueue.js`), which
  sorts by priority rank and stamps `queueOrder`. It supports a global call
  (`getScheduledQueue(store, undefined)` lists all projects), BUT the route
  forces a project via `resolveAndGuardProject`: with no `projectId` it
  returns the ACTIVE project's queue, never the global queue. Also note
  `getScheduledQueue` EXCLUDES `failed`, `cancelled`, `waiting_human`, and
  human-stage tasks (L52–70), while the chip number INCLUDES them — so chip
  count and queue length legitimately differ today.
- The exact interaction precedent is `BuildHashTrigger` +
  `ChangelogModal` (`frontend/src/components/layout/`): a right-rail
  element opening a dialog built on the shared accessible `Modal`
  (`frontend/src/components/Modal.jsx`: Escape/backdrop close, focus trap).
  `WidgetManagerModal` is a second `Modal` consumer.

## Survey synthesis (`SURVEY.md`)

All five survey questions are still unanswered (`"answers": {}`). The plan
therefore carries each question as a decision with a reversible default
(marked [D]), so implementation is unblocked and the operator can still
override before or during implementation:

| Survey Q | Decision carried by this plan |
|---|---|
| q1 — what should the queue number count? | [D] Keep the global open-task meaning for now; make the popup reconcile it (Step 4 + Step 9). Changing the count definition is deferred to Phase 4, conditional on q4. |
| q2 — what should each row show? | [D] Show all five surveyed fields: task name, position, project, current step, waiting/blocked reason. All are already present on `getScheduledQueue` items (`title`, `queueOrder`, `projectName`, `currentStageName`, `priorityReason`/`blockers`). |
| q3 — view-only vs actions? | [D] View-only list + click-a-row-opens-inspector (reuses the existing `setSelectedTask` pattern from the bar). No reorder/cancel — the scheduler owns order and there is no reorder API. |
| q4 — fix the number too, or popup only? | [D] Popup first (this plan's core), number-semantics fix as a separately-gated follow-up step once the popup provides evidence. This is the "make change easy, then make the change" split. |
| q5 — which queue number opens the popup? | [D] The bottom-bar chip only — it is the only queue number in the main UI. (Monitor KPI widgets show queue depth too, but only inside the monitor view.) |

If the operator answers the survey before implementation, the answers
override the [D] defaults. Biggest swing: q4 ("popup only" vs "fix the
number too") and q3 (full reorder/cancel would need a new backend API and
is currently out of scope).

## Approach — make change easy, then make the change

1. **Research spike first (Phase 0).** The one architectural unknown is the
   popup's data source: nothing today serves the GLOBAL ordered queue to
   the frontend (chip = global count, queue endpoints = project-scoped).
   Resolve this before building UI.
2. **Make change easy (Phase 1).** Extract the queue-list rendering and the
   queue-fetch logic into shared units so the popup reuses — not forks —
   the monitor's list. Keep every refactor behaviour-preserving with the
   existing tests green.
3. **Make the change (Phase 2).** Convert the chip to a button opening a
   `Modal` popup; wire the shared list into it.
4. **Then (Phase 4)** decide the count-semantics fix with popup evidence in
   hand — never bundled into the popup diff.

Big/risky work (data-source decision, shared seams) is deliberately first;
small UI wiring comes after the seams exist.

### Phase 0 — Research spike: pick the popup's data source (do first)

- **Step 1.** Confirm what `api.observabilityStatus(undefined)` returns for
  `.observability.queue` when no project filter is set (global or
  active-project?). Read the API route plus one backend test. No code
  changed.
- **Step 2.** Confirm `GET /tasks/queue` without `projectId` returns the

  `api/work/taskWorkRoutes.js`) and check the contract tests in
  `api/work/taskWorkRoutes.test.js` ("GET /tasks/queue") for constraints.

  - (a) If the observability queue already serves global order, reuse
    `api.observabilityStatus(undefined)` + existing refresh pattern (same as
    `ObservabilityDashboard.jsx`).
  - (b) Else, extend `GET /tasks/queue` with an explicit global mode (e.g.
    `?projectId=all`, mirroring the monitor's `selectedProjectId`
    convention) that calls `getScheduledQueue(store, undefined)`.
    Backend-only addition; no existing contract changes.

    chip-vs-list scope difference. Only if (a) and (b) are both rejected.

- Counts ALL open tasks across ALL projects
- Includes: failed, cancelled, waiting-human, paused, blocked
- Source: `engineState.openQueueDepth` (global count)
